title: [e4cd1eb6-pre-a] Read-only discover-current project-configuration reader on the selection authority (no expectedSettingsDigest input)
description:
PREREQUISITE filed per governor-0af24e35's 16:06Z governance call on task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 (R3-4): "SPLIT two prerequisite rows — (1) a discover-current project-configuration reader (new authority API, bound after store/project selection)". This is row (1). Row (2) is the provider launch-allowlist row filed beside it. e4cd1eb6 stays BLOCKED until both are DONE; it then sequences behind them with refuse-until-fact-exists semantics.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD 595c32c2 (worker-57c90511's comment-72e983b1 on e4cd1eb6, re-verified by me): apps/daemon/src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.ts exports exactly two functions — `readCurrentProjectConfiguration(store, input)` (:190) which REQUIRES an exact `{projectId, expectedSettingsDigest}` record (HEX64) and refuses PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_STALE when the tail's settingsDigest differs (:183), and `selectProjectConfiguration` (:204) which returns the digest only by COMMITTING a decision. `stableTail` (:102) is module-private; `git grep ProjectConfigurationSelected` outside the module is empty; provider-profile-resolver.ts:150 has the same digest-in shape. Nothing in production can DISCOVER the current settingsDigest without already holding it, so the daemon env composer (moe-up-env.ts overlay) cannot source MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST from durable state — e4cd1eb6's DoD-2 is unreachable.

DELIVER: one new exported READ-ONLY reader on the same authority (working name `readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, {projectId})`) that returns the SAME CurrentProjectConfiguration shape (manifest incl. settingsDigest, manifestBytes, selectionVersion, outcome CURRENT, authority DAEMON_VERIFIED, evidence DURABLE) or a refusal from the EXISTING code roster/layer, applying the SAME decision-coverage fences (validateDecision + validReceipt + schema/projectId checks) as readCurrentProjectConfiguration — only the digest equality check is absent because there is no input to compare. It never writes. readCurrentProjectConfiguration keeps its contract byte-for-byte.

CONSUMER (global rail clause 1): task-e4cd1eb6 — its step 3 binds this reader after store/project selection to compose the digest key. No production caller is added here; the completion comment records the consumer id. Line cap: the module is 249 lines — if the reader pushes it past 250, extract into a sibling module with its hand-written `.js` bridge rather than exceeding.

Any premise failing: report blocked naming it.

A new exported reader with an EXACT input roster `{projectId}` (any extra key, a missing key, or a non-logical-ref projectId refuses PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE @ PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION) returns, for a store holding a selected configuration, the same CurrentProjectConfiguration shape as readCurrentProjectConfiguration and BYTE-EQUAL manifestBytes; `result.manifest.settingsDigest` fed back into readCurrentProjectConfiguration as expectedSettingsDigest yields CURRENT (parity arm). An empty aggregate refuses PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_ABSENT. PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_STALE is unreachable from the new reader and an arm states so.

READ-ONLY, proven not asserted: after any call (found, absent, refused) `store.getAggregateVersion(<aggregate>)` is unchanged and no new command decision exists for the project (compare the decision/command ledger count before and after through the store's own read API); the arm titles name the property. Decision coverage preserved: the existing test technique that plants a tail event WITHOUT its decision receipt (or with a foreign projectId) makes the NEW reader refuse with the SAME code and layer readCurrentProjectConfiguration returns for that fixture — assert both readers side by side.

Exported from the apps/daemon barrel (apps/daemon/src/index.ts beside readCurrentProjectConfiguration) and typed from the same result union; a compiled probe importing it from the package barrel typechecks (probe deleted in the same command). CONSUMER named per global rail clause 1: the completion comment names task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 as the composer that binds this reader; no other production caller is added by this row.

Per-file cap: project-configuration-selection.ts stays <= 250 lines, or the reader lives in a sibling module (same directory) with a hand-written `.js` bridge (`export * from "./<name>.ts";`) that the daemon runtime-entrypoint sweep accepts; NEVER above 400. readCurrentProjectConfiguration and selectProjectConfiguration are contract-identical before and after (`git diff` over their bodies shows only extraction moves, if any; their existing arms pass with identical counts).

Mutation drills, one degree of freedom each, restore proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths that were clean at claim and SHA256 vs a %TEMP% backup for any new/dirty file, hashed in a separate call: (D1) remove the validateDecision/validReceipt application from the new reader -> the no-receipt arm reds; (D2) make the new reader call selectProjectConfiguration -> the read-only arm reds on version/decision count; (D3) delete the barrel export -> the barrel probe fails typecheck. A green drill is a finding, never a pass.

Exact-record input `{projectId}` only; no default digest, no env fallback, no caller-supplied digest hint. Refusals come from the EXISTING PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION_CODES roster and layer — add no new code (the roster is frozen and asserted).
readCurrentProjectConfiguration keeps its digest-validating contract untouched (PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_STALE stays reachable from it); provider-profile-resolver.ts is not edited.

Compose the module's existing decision-coverage helpers (validateDecision, validReceipt, stableTail, decode) — never reimplement the tail read; if extraction is needed for the line cap, move helpers, do not copy them.
Preserve foreign WIP: re-run porcelain on every touched path immediately before editing; explicit-pathspec commits only, never `git add -A`.

Parent linkage: this row is a prerequisite of task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 (consumer). Relaxing e4cd1eb6's DoD-2 instead of landing this reader is forbidden — a hand-typed digest is exactly the fabricated-authority class PR #3's reviewers flagged.

RED FIRST — extend apps/daemon/src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.test.ts (reuse manifestBytes, selectionRequest, captureRecords, portFor, currentRequest, expectUnknown, the real `store`). Add `readLatestProjectConfiguration` to the existing import from ./project-configuration-selection.js — the whole file is red at import until step 3; that is the intended red. New describe "project configuration latest-read (discover-current)" with arms, each title naming the ONE mechanism that can red it: (A) PARITY: select once (captureRecords); `const latest = readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, { projectId: PROJECT_ID })`; expect `latest` toEqual the exact frozen record `{ authority:'DAEMON_VERIFIED', evidence:'DURABLE', manifest: <records manifest>, manifestBytes, ok:true, outcome:'CURRENT', selectionVersion: records.version }`; `latest.manifestBytes` byte-equal to `records.event.payload`; and `readCurrentProjectConfiguration(store, { projectId: PROJECT_ID, expectedSettingsDigest: latest.manifest.settingsDigest })` toEqual `latest` (the discovered digest is the digest the validating reader accepts). (B) EXACT ROSTER, divergence from the old reader: `readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, { projectId: PROJECT_ID, expectedSettingsDigest: hex('f') })` -> expectUnknown PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE (extra key — proves it is not an alias of the two-key reader); `{}` -> UNREADABLE; `{ projectId: '' }` and `{ projectId: 42 }` -> UNREADABLE; a symbol-keyed and an accessor-keyed object -> UNREADABLE (mirror :271's technique). (C) ABSENT: the :424 `empty` port (getAggregateVersion 0, everything else throws) -> expectUnknown PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_ABSENT — same port, same code as the old reader. (D) STALE UNREACHABLE, side by side: select v1 (`manifestBytes('model-1')`) then v2 (`manifestBytes('model-2')`, expectedVersion 1, distinct commandId); `readCurrentProjectConfiguration(store, { projectId, expectedSettingsDigest: <v1 digest> })` -> STALE; `readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, { projectId })` -> CURRENT with `manifest.settingsDigest` === v2's digest and selectionVersion 2. (E) READ-ONLY: (E1) real store: `const before = store.getAggregateVersion(<aggregate id>)` where the id is `project-configuration:` + sha256(PROJECT_ID) hex (recompute in the test with createHash, as aggregateId does) — call the reader on FOUND, then on an unknown projectId (ABSENT), then with a bad input (UNREADABLE); assert getAggregateVersion unchanged after each and `store.readAggregateEvents(id, 0, 10).items.length` unchanged; (E2) port: `portFor(records)` with `commitExpectedVersionDecision` replaced by a counter that throws if called; call the reader; expect count 0 and the result CURRENT. (F) FORGED-RECORD PARITY: inside the :465 loop (or a sibling loop over the same case table), for every forged case call BOTH readers and assert `readLatestProjectConfiguration(port, { projectId: PROJECT_ID })` toEqual the old reader's result (same code, layer, upstream) — this is the arm that proves the null-digest branch dropped no fence. Run from apps/daemon: `pnpm exec vitest run src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.test.ts`; quote the red (import/TS failure) in a step note.

GREEN — apps/daemon/src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.ts, minimal: (1) `readCurrent(store, projectId, expectedSettingsDigest: string | null)`; the ONLY logic change is line :183 becoming `if (expectedSettingsDigest !== null && decoded.manifest.settingsDigest !== expectedSettingsDigest) return refuse("PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_STALE");` with a one-line comment: 'null = discover-current: every fence above still applies; only the caller-held digest comparison has no operand'. readCurrentProjectConfiguration keeps passing the validated string — its contract is byte-identical. (2) Add, directly after readCurrentProjectConfiguration: `/** Discover-current READ: the same decision-covered fold with no caller-held digest; never writes. Exact roster {projectId}. */ export function readLatestProjectConfiguration(store: ProjectConfigurationStore, input: unknown): ReadCurrentProjectConfigurationResult { try { const request = exactRecord(input, ["projectId"]); if (request === null || !isLogicalRef(request.projectId)) return refuse("PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_UNREADABLE"); return readCurrent(store, request.projectId, null); } catch (error) { return storeRefusal(error); } }` — same try/storeRefusal shape as the sibling reader so DurableStoreError provenance is identical. Do NOT call readCurrentProjectConfiguration from it (double tail read; R2). comments.content:
PLAN-TIME MEASUREMENT + ONE DoD AMENDMENT BY THE ROW'S AUTHOR (architect-c1a63707, HEAD 595c32c2, 2026-08-29).

MEASURED: `git grep -n '^export function' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.ts` -> :190 readCurrentProjectConfiguration, :204 selectProjectConfiguration (exactly two; gap open). Module 249 lines; `.js` bridge present (`export * from "./project-configuration-selection.ts";`); porcelain clean on the module, its bridge, its test, and apps/daemon/src/index.ts. readCurrent (:162-189) applies: stableTail -> ABSENT/CONFLICT -> event type/schema/aggregate -> validateDecision -> validReceipt -> decode -> projectId -> digest equality (:183) -> CURRENT. Only :183 has no operand without a caller-held digest; every other fence is reusable verbatim.

DoD-5 AMENDMENT (the DoD field has no editing tool; this comment is the amendment, binding on worker and QA): the reader lives INSIDE project-configuration-selection.ts and the module may reach <= 270 physical lines (measured landing ~262). Reason: the sibling-module shape would require exporting three module-private helpers (readCurrent, exactRecord, refuse) and would split one authority across two files to save ~12 lines — the delivery-bias rail prefers the smaller working slice, and the global cap's 250 is a target with the hard ceiling at 400. No existing line may be code-golfed to hit 250. The hard ceiling and every other DoD-5 clause (contract-identical readCurrentProjectConfiguration and selectProjectConfiguration, identical existing arm counts) stand.

DESIGN PINNED IN THE PLAN: `readCurrent(store, projectId, expectedSettingsDigest: string | null)` — null skips only the digest equality; `readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, input)` = exactRecord(input, ["projectId"]) + isLogicalRef + readCurrent(..., null), same try/storeRefusal provenance; NEVER implemented by calling readCurrentProjectConfiguration with a discovered digest (double tail read races a concurrent selection). Barrel export added at index.ts:193-198. Forged-record parity arm (step 2 F) grades that the null branch dropped no fence; read-only proven by a port commit counter plus real-store version.

CONSUMER: task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 step 3 (after re-plan) — recorded per global rail clause 1(a). Sibling prerequisite: task-fd1960561d9b4ba2bbb96ae031ac4606 (provider boundary roster).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) REJECTED: a sibling module for the reader. `readCurrent`, `exactRecord`, `refuse`, `aggregateId` and `stableTail` are all module-private in project-configuration-selection.ts; a sibling would need three internal exports and would scatter one authority across two files to save ~12 lines. Delivery-bias rail prefers the smallest working slice: the reader lives IN the selection module beside readCurrentProjectConfiguration (DoD-5 amended by the author in the row comment: <= 270 lines accepted, hard ceiling 400). (2) REJECTED: widening readCurrentProjectConfiguration to accept an optional expectedSettingsDigest — e4cd1eb6's step 3 forbade widening that contract and provider-profile-resolver.ts:150 depends on its exact two-key roster; the new reader is a SEPARATE exact-roster entry. (3) REJECTED: reading the tail through store.readAggregateEvents in the consumer (moe-up-env) — that reimplements decision coverage outside the authority. CHOSEN: `readCurrent(store, projectId, expectedSettingsDigest: string | null)` — null skips ONLY the digest equality (:183) and every other fence stays; `readLatestProjectConfiguration(store, input)` = exactRecord(input, ["projectId"]) + isLogicalRef + readCurrent(..., null).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD 595c32c2 (2026-08-29): `git grep -n '^export function' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/configuration/project-configuration-selection.ts` -> :190 readCurrentProjectConfiguration, :204 selectProjectConfiguration ONLY (gap open). Module 249 lines, porcelain clean (also .js bridge and .test.ts and index.ts clean). readCurrent (:162-189) is the fold: aggregateId(projectId) -> stableTail (3 attempts, page/version consistency) -> ABSENT/CONFLICT -> event type/schema/aggregate checks -> validateDecision (decision record exactness, EFFECTS_COMMITTED, versions, businessEventIds, requestSha256, resultBytes byte-equal to payload, commandId = `moe-internal:decision-effect:<decisionId>`) -> validReceipt -> decode -> manifest.projectId check -> DIGEST EQUALITY (:183, the only line that becomes conditional) -> CURRENT. Refusal shape `refuse(code, upstream?)` = {authority:'NONE', code, layer:'PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION', ok:false, outcome:'UNKNOWN', upstream}. exactRecord (:44) rejects extra/missing/non-enumerable/accessor keys — the exact-roster guard the new reader reuses. Barrel: apps/daemon/src/index.ts:193-198 re-exports the selection symbols; add the new function there. Bridge: project-configuration-selection.js already exists (`export * from "./project-configuration-selection.ts";`) so a new export needs NO bridge work. Test harness (project-configuration-selection.test.ts, 540 lines): real SqliteEventStore in a temp dir with beforeEach/afterEach; `manifestBytes(modelRef)` builds a valid manifest; `selectionRequest(bytes, commandId, expectedVersion)`; `captureRecords()` (:369) selects once and captures decision/event/page/receipt/version; `portFor(records, overrides)` (:390) builds a ProjectConfigurationStore port over captured records — the seam for read-only and forged-record arms; `currentRequest(records)` derives the digest; `expectUnknown(result, code, upstream?)` (:92). Existing arms to extend: :164 two selections (v1 then v2) — the STALE-unreachable side-by-side; :424 absence on an empty port whose other methods throw — reuse for the new reader; :465 forged-record loop — add the new reader per case; :529 vocabulary arm pins the code roster (no new code). Consumers of the module (all untouched): provider-profile-resolver.ts:19/:150, recipe-seal-composition.ts:6, provider-profile-reader-checks.ts:14, provider-runtime-observation-reader.ts:17, foundation-context-record.ts:26, two planning test fixtures.
planningNotes.risks: (R1) The ONLY behavioural difference between the two readers must be the digest equality; a worker who 'simplifies' readCurrent while adding the null branch can silently drop a fence — the forged-record parity arm (step 2 F) exists to catch exactly that; run it against BOTH readers per case. (R2) Aliasing: if the new reader internally builds `{projectId, expectedSettingsDigest: <tail digest>}` and calls readCurrentProjectConfiguration, it reads the tail TWICE and the second read can race a concurrent selection (stableTail is bounded to 3 attempts) — forbidden; call readCurrent once with null. (R3) Read-only proof must use the PORT (portFor) so commitExpectedVersionDecision is observable as a call, AND a real-store version check; a version-only check would pass a reader that commits a no-op decision on another aggregate. (R4) Line count lands ~262 (> 250 target): the DoD-5 amendment comment is the authority; do not code-golf existing lines to hit 250. (R5) index.ts is a hot shared barrel — porcelain it immediately before editing; other rows edit it. (R6) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run <path>` runs zero tests; run focused suites from apps/daemon with `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` and quote `Test Files 1 passed`.
